source.title: Do VLMs Have Bad Eyes? Diagnosing Compositional Failures via Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Ashwath Vaithinathan Aravindan; Abha Jha; M. Kulkarni

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates superposition in a pretrained vision encoder using neuron-activation analysis and embedding measures rather than the original toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on neuron-level feature sharing, embedding overlap, compositional localization, and associations between its superposition score and embedding measures. It does not test sparse-feature capacity pressure, sparsity-dependent transitions, feature importance, SAE recovery, or feature dimensionality. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study studies a CLIP vision transformer, not a toy model or an LLM. It finds that some MLP neurons respond to several attributes and calls this superposition without testing it. It does not test capacity pressure, sparsity, geometry, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality. It then uses the label to explain compositional (binding) failures. No result bears on a version as stated, so the findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right but understates the authors. Their conclusion says the findings 'establish superposition as a key bottleneck' for compositionality, and the abstract says it 'directly hinders' compositional representation. They also acknowledge that the S–D and S–M correlations are weak and that a causal link needs future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a pretrained CLIP vision encoder, synthetic shape images, neuron feature-affinity/entropy analysis, and embedding-distance and misclassification measures; it does not train the original sparse-feature toy network or test its sparsity and capacity regimes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that later-layer self-attention can mix information across spatial tokens, affecting localization of neuron activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Some low-entropy MLP neurons in the CLIP-ViT-L/14 vision encoder respond to several shape, colour and position attributes. Their entropies (3.34–3.4 bits, against a 4-bit maximum) show only modest selectivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual MLP neurons in a pretrained ViT vision encoder respond to multiple visual attributes in a synthetic-shapes setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors' neuron-sharing score S for feature pairs is weakly associated with smaller embedding-centroid distance and higher nearest-centroid misclassification. No correlation value is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In CLIP, attribute pairs that share neurons more are weakly less separable in the output embedding.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-image Grad-CAM examples show correct localization for matching prompts. They show split or scattered attention for an absent colour–shape conjunction and for a spatial-relation prompt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLIP shows attribute-binding and spatial-relation grounding failures in qualitative Grad-CAM examples.

fits_no_version.finding: A t-SNE plot of CLIP embeddings shows mostly separable CIFAR-10 classes, with some overlap among animal classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLIP embeddings of semantically similar CIFAR-10 classes partially overlap.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
record.problems: The study is limited to one CLIP model and a small synthetic dataset of 500 images. The Grad-CAM findings are qualitative. The authors acknowledge that the reported correlations are weak and that a direct causal link has not been established. No uncertainty estimates or control comparisons are reported for the relevant measurements.

untested.parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry: none of these are tested.
Capacity competition and the dedicated-vs-shared allocation by importance are not tested. Polysemanticity is simply assumed to be superposition.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity are not examined. The study assumes polysemantic neurons are evidence of superposition.
No LLMs are studied, and no SAE or dictionary recovery is attempted. The only neuron evidence is polysemantic ViT neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' conflicts with its own finding that every version is untested. The study equates polysemantic neurons with superposition without testing capacity or geometry, and it uses a vision transformer, not an LLM, so V4 as worded does not apply. The affinity values do not sum to 1 (images contain several objects), and the 'low-entropy' neurons are near the maximum entropy. The study uses a single model, 500 synthetic images, no controls and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test limited-capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or sharing by less important features.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure or whether it is evidence of superposition.
Studies a CLIP vision encoder, not LLMs; it does not test features spread across neurons or SAE recovery.
Does not use or evaluate SAEs or test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical.
Does not distinguish one-dimensional feature directions from multidimensional features.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Projected pooler outputs into 2D with t-SNE and inspected class clustering.
rows.measure: Visual overlap among image-embedding class clusters
rows.value: Class-specific clusters were clearly separable for most categories; some overlap was observed among semantically similar categories (e.g., dog, cat, horse, deer).
rows.note: The authors describe the overlap as hinting at embedding-level superposition; the visualization does not directly measure feature directions.
rows.check: A qualitative t-SNE plot of class clusters cannot show superposition of feature directions. The authors only say the overlap 'hints at' superposition.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14, 16th transformer block, 563rd neuron
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature affinities and patch-wise activations for the neuron.
rows.measure: Feature affinities and responses to multiple visual features
rows.value: Entropy 3.36 (0.18 %ile); top features Circle (0.57), Pink (0.57), Square (0.53), Top-Left (0.4), Red (0.3). The text describes strong activation for circles, squares, pink, and red, and low activation for unrelated features and an image containing only a triangle.
rows.note: The authors interpret the neuron as responding to multiple visual concepts; this does not establish a capacity mechanism or a feature-direction geometry.
rows.check: This shows a multi-attribute (polysemantic) neuron in a ViT, not an LLM, with no capacity or geometry test. Entropy 3.36 out of a maximum of 4 bits (16 features) is fairly spread even for a 'low-entropy' neuron. The state is observed only for polysemantic response, not for superposition.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14, 22nd transformer block, 447th neuron
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature affinities for the neuron.
rows.value: Entropy 3.34 (0.08 %ile); top features Circle (0.6), Middle (0.6), Pentagon (0.47), Pink (0.37), Top-Left (0.3).
rows.note: The table reports affinities to multiple features for this neuron.
rows.check: Polysemantic response in a ViT neuron. Entropy 3.34 is close to the 4-bit maximum. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14, 18th transformer block, 466th neuron
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature affinities for the neuron.
rows.value: Entropy 3.4 (0.38 %ile); top features Pink (0.63), Black (0.4), Square (0.37), Bottom-Right (0.37), Pentagon (0.3).
rows.note: The table reports affinities to multiple features for this neuron.
rows.check: Polysemantic response in a ViT neuron. Entropy 3.4 is close to the 4-bit maximum. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Compared the superposition score for feature pairs with cluster-center distance.
rows.measure: Relationship between superposition score S and cluster-center distance D
rows.value: The text reports that feature pairs with higher S exhibit smaller D; it characterizes the correlation as weak.
rows.note: The plotted values are not reported numerically in the text.
rows.check: This is an association between the authors' own S score and embedding distance. It is weak by the authors' account, and no correlation value or uncertainty is given. It is not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Compared the superposition score for feature pairs with misclassification rate.
rows.measure: Relationship between superposition score S and misclassification rate M
rows.value: The text reports that higher-S feature pairs have higher M; it characterizes the correlation as weak.
rows.note: The plotted values are not reported numerically in the text.
rows.check: This is an association between S and misclassification. It is weak by the authors' account and given without numbers. It is not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Compared Grad-CAM localization for a text prompt matching the image with localization for a prompt whose conjunction was absent.
rows.value: The model correctly localizes the green circle.
rows.check: This is a Grad-CAM binding result. It measures compositional grounding, not superposition, so its state relative to the claim is cannot_determine.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Examined Grad-CAM localization for a prompt describing a color-shape conjunction absent from the image.
rows.value: Attention is split between the red square and the green circle, although there is no green square in the image.
rows.note: The authors describe attention to separate partial matches rather than the absent conjunction.
rows.check: This is a Grad-CAM binding failure, a different construct from superposition. It is qualitative, from a single image.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Examined Grad-CAM localization for an object prompt.
rows.value: The model identifies the dog and focuses primarily on the animal, with concentrated activation around the snout, paws, and face.
rows.check: This is a Grad-CAM localization result and does not bear on superposition.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Examined Grad-CAM localization for a spatially compositional prompt.
rows.value: Attention is scattered across the dog, background, and pot regions.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as a limitation in grounded relational or positional understanding.
rows.check: This is a Grad-CAM spatial-relation failure and does not bear on superposition.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
